costBasis.measured: The halted population run completed 9 candidates for $0.04655 total - mean $0.00517 each, mean wall-clock 184 s.

cohorts.name: PREVIOUSLY-SUCCESSFUL CONTROLS (regression)
cohorts.why: All 9 are single-key, so R1 does not change their operative text by a single character. The negative control.
cohorts.passCriterion: 9/9 COMPLETED, with rule counts and output hashes comparable to the pre-change run. Any change here means R1 touched something it should not have.

cohorts.name: MANUFACTURED-LONG CASES (the target)
cohorts.why: Every one TIMED OUT or failed in the real runs. Simulated post-change: 1 shard each, max sequential calls 16 -> 14.
cohorts.passCriterion: at least 3 of 4 COMPLETED within 480 s (7.2(k) is the designated flush-proviso risk case from legal case E/F and may legitimately require review); every cited source span must lie inside the anchor span.

cohorts.name: FALSE-CREDIT SAFETY
candidates: 7.9 - the CONMED parent sections that are themselves candidates and are the text being appended
cohorts.why: These are the propositions the children were borrowing; after the change only these candidates may emit them. CONMED has no false-credit control of its own, so this is the CONMED-side proxy. The 14 DSGR controls are re-checked ZERO-COST by replaying the existing deterministic control check, never by new model calls.
cohorts.passCriterion: each parent still compiles its own chapeau rule, and the deterministic re-check shows 14/14 DSGR controls still protected.

cohorts.name: DUAL-KEY BEFORE/AFTER PAIRS
cohorts.why: Dual-key rows that TIMED OUT or hit PROVIDER_FAILURE in the halted run - a direct before/after on the same candidates.
cohorts.passCriterion: at least 2 of 3 COMPLETED, versus 0 of 3 before.
